newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Sept prelim industrial output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Sept prelim industrial output.

text.p: The following is a selection of analysts' reactions to Japan's September preliminary industrial production data released on Tuesday, which showed a 1.0 percent rise from a month earlier on a seasonally adjusted basis.
Industrial output for the July-September quarter grew 1.5 percent quarter-on-quarter, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry said.
JASON JAMES, STRATEGIST AT JAMES CAPEL, TOKYO
"They are extremely encouraging. We were at the top end of the range, looking at 0.5 percent growth month-on-month. They beat our expectations."

James told RFTV that two factors were currently driving industrial production figures -- that the inventory adjustment process was essentially over, and that demand was kicking in before a consumption tax increase scheduled from April 1997.
"It shows the benefits from low interest rates and weaker yen. The potential for the export market has gone up and the economy is gradually recovering.

"But we have to see further evidence that October (data) does come out strong before we can revise this view that the economy is gradually recovering because there are still a lot of constraints in the Japanese economy."
RICHARD WERNER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, JARDINE FLEMING
"The figures were very strong, basically, as expected, because the economy is recovering fairly significantly and that means that production is also recovering.
Werner said that the year-on-year figure of 3.4 percent was far above the consensus of 2.3 percent. He said Jardine Fleming had forecast 3.0 percent.
